page: Amazon Web Services g6.48xlarge is an accelerated computing instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The platform features 192 vCPUs across 96 physical cores based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. System memory totals 768.0 GB of DDR4 running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB per core. Acceleration hardware includes eight NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPUs equipped with 179 GB of aggregate VRAM. Local high-speed storage is bundled via 7520 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, complemented by a 100 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the upper deciles for both multi-threaded compute and parallel graphics. The system recorded a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 286988.18 and a PassMark CPU score of 109870.16. Small-block cached read memory bandwidth reached 10516.05 GB/sec, while large-block uncached memory read bandwidth attained 254.22 GB/sec. Parallel execution capabilities are reflected in top-tier results for Clang software compilation at 57980.0, ray tracing at 137807.0, and high-throughput memory caching with Redis SET operations yielding 159.29 million operations per second.

Machine learning evaluations highlight high throughput during token generation and prompt ingestion. Prompt processing throughput reaches 11797.22 tokens per second on a small 135M parameter model, 2812.24 tokens per second on a medium 7B model, and 310.84 tokens per second on a 70B parameter architecture. Text generation rates range from 378.85 tokens per second on small models to 5.8 tokens per second on large 70B models. The dense multi-GPU design, coupled with 7520 GB NVMe storage and 100 Gbps networking, aligns with deep learning inference, video processing, 3D graphics rendering, and data-intensive computing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services g6.48xlarge is an accelerated computing instance within the AWS Nitro architecture, engineered for intensive parallel graphics and machine learning workloads. The system features 192 vCPUs across 96 physical AMD EPYC 7R13 processor cores operating at 3.4 GHz, 768 GB of DDR4 memory, and 7520 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Hardware acceleration is provided by eight NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L4 GPUs delivering a combined 179 GB of video memory, complemented by 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic and real-world benchmarks position this instance in the top tier for multi-core compute throughput, Clang compilation, ray tracing, and Redis operations exceeding 159 million transactions per second. For artificial intelligence pipelines, the eight L4 accelerators enable high-throughput prompt processing and generation across small, medium, and large language models. The dense multi-GPU configuration and fast local storage support distributed LLM inference, video transcoding, visual rendering, and data-intensive computational tasks.
